book.title: crlibm 1.0beta5: the sinh correct-rounding claim
book.description: The manual's Table 1 marks sinh 'complete', which the manual defines as correct rounding over the whole floating-point input range. Each directed-rounding entry is a row over the deposited witness set. The rows are finite-grid conformance: a mismatch refutes the claim, a pass on the sample does not establish it over the whole range.

provenance.upstream: crlibm archive SHA-256 79d626f9515fccdbc724e8b74cbf848331317b1891ef22aaaf6a195e20bbbfe5; docs/latex/0_getting-started.tex line 149 and lines 173-177
provenance.reference: mpmath 1.4.1 at 60 significant decimal digits, with the IEEE 754 clause 7.4 overflow rule
provenance.measured: crlibm 1.0beta5 built on x86-64 Linux, gcc 15.2, --enable-sse2 --disable-mpfr --disable-double-extended; FLT_EVAL_METHOD=0
provenance.note: The witness set is 422 arguments: the named input, its neighbours, the mirror, and scans of the overflow tail. The manual's claim is over the whole floating-point input range; 422 arguments sample it.

domain.description: the whole floating-point input range, the domain the manual's definition of 'complete' states

claims.route: the four directed-rounding entry points sinh_rn, sinh_ru, sinh_rd, sinh_rz
assumptions: correct rounding follows IEEE 754 clause 7.4, so an overflow returns the largest finite magnitude in the required direction, not infinity
the expected bits are computed from mpmath at 60 significant decimal digits with the clause 7.4 rule

source.document: crlibm docs/latex/0_getting-started.tex line 149; the definition is lines 173-177

claims.subject: the bit identity of each sinh entry with the correctly rounded result

registrations.sentence: sinh & sinh\_rn & sinh\_ru & sinh\_rd & sinh\_rz & complete & complete (paper)\\ \hline
registrations.scope: the first state column; 'complete' is defined by the supporting sentence

supporting.sentence: The first indicates the state of the search for worst cases for correct rounding \cite{LMT98,Lef2000}. If it indicates ``complete'', it means that the function is guaranteed to return correct rounding on its whole floating-point input range.

rows.statement: sinh_rn returns the correctly rounded result at each of the 422 sampled inputs
rows.subject: sinh_rn in binary64

domain.description: the 422-argument witness set: the named inputs, their neighbours, the mirror, and scans of the overflow tail

assumptions: the expected bits use the clause 7.4 overflow rule
rows.notes: Round-to-nearest is correct at the overflow witness because the exact value lies above the round-to-nearest overflow midpoint.

rows.statement: sinh_ru returns the correctly rounded result at each of the 422 sampled inputs
rows.subject: sinh_ru in binary64

domain.description: the 422-argument witness set: the named inputs, their neighbours, the mirror, and scans of the overflow tail

assumptions: the expected bits use the clause 7.4 overflow rule
rows.notes: Fails at the negated witness: -inf where -DBL_MAX is required.

rows.statement: sinh_rd returns the correctly rounded result at each of the 422 sampled inputs
rows.subject: sinh_rd in binary64

domain.description: the 422-argument witness set: the named inputs, their neighbours, the mirror, and scans of the overflow tail

assumptions: the expected bits use the clause 7.4 overflow rule
rows.notes: Fails at the positive witness 0x408633ce8fb9f87e: +inf where +DBL_MAX is required.

rows.statement: sinh_rz returns the correctly rounded result at each of the 422 sampled inputs
rows.subject: sinh_rz in binary64

domain.description: the 422-argument witness set: the named inputs, their neighbours, the mirror, and scans of the overflow tail

assumptions: the expected bits use the clause 7.4 overflow rule
rows.notes: Fails at both witnesses, because sinh_rz delegates to sinh_rd for positive and sinh_ru for negative inputs.
